column6: Item wording
We keep a written or electronic record of the quantity of raw material we take in each season.
We write down how much of what we handle is rejected, downgraded or lost.
column7: The one item quoted in your manuscript.

column6: We record what happens to the material that does not become saleable product — where it goes and who takes it.
We work out what the material we lose or reject cost us to buy or to produce.
We know what the rejected or lost material would have earned had it been sold as product.
We keep the cost of losses separate from our general operating costs rather than absorbing it into overall cost.
Before deciding whether to recover a by-product or residue, we estimate what it could earn.
column7: New dimension; expert disagreement concentrated here.

column6: We compare the cost of recovering a residue against the cost of disposing of it.
When we consider equipment or capacity for processing residues, we work out whether the investment would pay back.
Partners we deal with can see how much material is rejected or lost at our stage.
We can see how much material is rejected or lost at the stages before and after us.
Information about recoverable residues and by-products reaches the people who could use them, in time for them to act.
Information about material flows and losses in this chain is accurate and reliable enough to base a decision on.
We can see how the money paid for the final product is divided among the actors in this chain.
column7: Price rather than material information — most likely to behave differently.

column6: It is clear which party is answerable when material is lost or spoiled between us and our partners.
Our partners and we jointly check the quantities and quality recorded when material changes hands.
What counts as an acceptable level of loss is agreed and recorded with our partners.
We are able to take part in decisions that affect how material and losses are handled in this chain.
Our views are taken into account when the terms of trade in this chain are set.
Commitments our partners make about handling, collection or payment are honoured, and there are consequences if they are not.
column7: Low ρA here attenuates the interaction directly.

column6: We plan jointly with partners how material that would otherwise be wasted will be collected and moved.
We coordinate the timing of our operations with partners so that recoverable material is handled before it deteriorates.
We share equipment, storage or transport with partners for handling residues and by-products.
We and our partners exchange the information needed to route recoverable material to where it can be used.
column7: Watch for HTMT overlap with CIT.

column6: We agree with partners in advance how the proceeds from recovered material will be shared.
We work together with partners to find new uses for material that used to be discarded.
Income earned from selling by-products or residues that were previously discarded.
Savings from reusing material internally instead of buying new.
The price we realise for our main product.
Reduction in the cost of disposing of waste.
Reduction in the quantity of material leaving our operation as waste.
Reduction in the share of what we handle that is lost or spoiled.
Reduction in the energy and water used per unit of product.
Reduction in the quantity of residues sent to landfill, burned or dumped.
The share of the value from recovered material that reaches the producers who supplied it.
column7: Weak SOC weight is a FINDING, not a failure.

column6: Employment or paid work created by handling and processing recovered material.
Fairness with which the gains from reducing losses are shared among the actors in this chain.
We use digital tools — mobile apps, spreadsheets or software — to record the quantities we handle.

column6: Material we handle can be traced back to its source using our records or codes.
We can exchange records of quantities and quality with our partners electronically.
Government or industry bodies provide us with useful guidance on reducing losses and using residues.
Training and technical advice on handling and processing residues are available to us.
Financial support or subsidy is available for equipment that would let us process residues.
